items.followUp: Differentiate between an atom and an ion.

accept: takes part in a chemical reaction
may or may not exist independently
rubric.why: These features define an atom and distinguish it from a particle that must exist independently.
rubric.description: Defines an atom as the smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction; it may or may not exist independently.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying an atom as a particle of an element involved in chemical reactions, including the fact that it may not exist independently.

accept: smallest particle of an element or compound
rubric.why: Independent existence and retention of the substance’s properties are defining features of a molecule.
rubric.description: Defines a molecule as the smallest particle of an element or compound that can exist independently and retain its chemical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a molecule as an independently existing particle that retains the properties of the substance.

modelAnswer: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction; it may or may not exist independently.
A molecule is the smallest particle of an element or compound that can exist independently and retains the chemical properties of the substance.

items.followUp: Complete the nuclear equation: ___ + ___ → ¹⁴₆C + ¹₁H.

rubric.why: These are the reactant nuclei required to produce carbon-12 and a neutron while conserving nucleon and proton numbers.
rubric.description: Identifies the reactants as ¹¹₅B and ²₁H.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing both correct reactant isotopes.

rubric.why: The completed equation conserves both mass number and atomic number.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced nuclear equation: ¹¹₅B + ²₁H → ¹²₆C + ¹₀n.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for completing the equation correctly, with mass and atomic numbers conserved.

items.followUp: How are elements arranged in groups in the periodic table?

rubric.why: A period is a horizontal row in the periodic table.
rubric.description: Identifies periods as horizontal rows in the periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that periods are horizontal rows.

accept: same number of occupied electron shells
rubric.why: These are key features of the arrangement of elements across a period.
rubric.description: States that atomic number increases across a period or that elements in the same period have the same number of occupied electron shells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct feature.

modelAnswer: Elements are arranged in horizontal rows called periods.
Across a period, atomic number increases, and elements in the same period have the same number of occupied electron shells.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and state a commonly used unit for it.

rubric.why: Removing an electron from an isolated gaseous atom is the defining process for ionization energy.
rubric.description: Defines ionization energy as the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition, including removal of an electron from a gaseous atom.

rubric.why: Ionization energy is commonly expressed per mole of atoms.
rubric.description: Gives the unit as kJ mol⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the unit kJ mol⁻¹.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.

items.followUp: What is meant by a polar covalent bond?

rubric.why: Equal sharing of the bonding electron pair is the defining feature of a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: States that the bonded atoms share the bonding electron pair equally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonding electrons are shared equally.

rubric.why: Equal sharing means the bond has no charge separation; identical atoms have the same electronegativity.
rubric.description: Identifies the absence of bond polarity, or notes that the bond is typically between identical atoms with the same electronegativity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that there is no charge separation or that the bonded atoms are identical/have the same electronegativity.

modelAnswer: A non-polar covalent bond is formed when the bonded atoms share the bonding electron pair equally.
There is no separation of charge across the bond; it commonly forms between identical atoms with the same electronegativity.
